verified.validation_type: strict ARM compilation and ARM instruction simulation of original C++ modules; no hardware or game

test_validity: The temporal ordering is a targeted stale-sample model, not an arbitrary wall-clock rollback. A command is accepted at timestamp t, representing the callback recording micros() after the main loop captured its local `now`; tick is then called at t-1 (one microsecond older) and is expected not to expire the timer. The wrap test places t near UINT32_MAX, uses a one-microsecond-old sample, and checks exactly the before/at modular deadline. The later-command case repeats the one-microsecond ordering for cmd2/cmd3/cmd4 and verifies the timer is preserved until its intended 400ms deadline. These are coherent models of the proposed callback-after-sample interleaving and wrap-safe elapsed-time logic.
interpretation: The three targeted tests fail in the current Io4State implementation exactly where the stale earlier `now` should be tolerated, while the pre-existing 11 module groups pass. This independently confirms that the pure Io4State model expires a nonzero timeout when tick receives a timestamp one microsecond earlier than last_command_us. Combined with the hardware units 1/4/255 diagnostic and confirmed TinyUSB IRQ/task path, the race hypothesis is strongly supported. This is still a software model result, not direct capture of hardware callback/tick timestamps; it does not alone prove that interleaving caused the board observation or validate any firmware fix.
